items.prompt: What is the SI unit of electric charge?

options.label: Farad
Coulomb
Volt
Ampere

rubric: The coulomb is the SI unit of charge.
The ampere is the unit of current (coulombs per second), which is the most common confusion.

items.prompt: Two protons are held close together. What is the electric force between them?

options.label: Repulsive
Attractive
Zero
Alternating

rubric: Like charges repel, and both protons are positive.
Choosing attractive confuses the gravitational rule with the rule for like charges.

items.prompt: Which equation is Ohm's law for a resistor?

options.label: V = I^2 R
V = I R
V = I / R
V = R / I

rubric: Ohm's law states that voltage equals current times resistance.
V = I^2 R is confused with the power formula.

items.prompt: Which law states that a changing magnetic flux through a loop induces an emf in the loop?

options.label: Faraday's law
Gauss's law
Ampere's law
Coulomb's law

rubric: Faraday's law links induced emf to the rate of change of flux.
Gauss's and Ampere's laws describe the sources of static fields, not induction.

items.prompt: Electric field lines around an isolated positive point charge point in which direction?

options.label: Away from the charge
Toward the charge
Parallel to each other
In circles around it

rubric: Field lines start on positive charges and point outward.
Circular lines describe magnetic field lines around a current, not electric field lines of a point charge.

items.prompt: Which of the following are among Maxwell's equations (in their usual named forms)? Select all that apply.

options.label: Newton's third law
Gauss's law for electric fields
Ohm's law
Faraday's law of induction
Gauss's law for magnetic fields

rubric: The usual named forms are Gauss's law for E, Gauss's law for B, Faraday's law and the Ampere-Maxwell law.
Ohm's law is a material relation and Newton's third law is mechanics, so neither is one of Maxwell's equations.

items.prompt: A technician wants to measure how much charge passes through a resistor each second. She connects a meter in series with the resistor in a working circuit. Which quantity does this meter measure, and in what unit?

options.label: Current, in amperes
Resistance, in ohms
Voltage, in volts
Charge, in coulombs

rubric: Charge flow per second is current, measured in amperes with a series ammeter.
Voltage is measured in parallel across a component, and total charge is a different quantity from a rate.

items.prompt: Why does a rubbed, negatively charged balloon stick to a neutral wall?

options.label: The wall carries a net positive charge from the start
The balloon's charge shifts wall charges, so nearby wall surface is attracted
Rubbing makes the balloon magnetic, so it sticks to the wall
Neutral objects always attract any charged object equally

rubric: The balloon polarises the wall, leaving the nearer surface positive, so attraction exceeds repulsion.
The wall is neutral, and the effect is electric, not magnetic.

items.prompt: The distance between two point charges is doubled. What happens to the electric force between them?

options.label: It stays the same
It becomes one quarter as large
It becomes four times as large
It becomes half as large

rubric: Coulomb's force follows an inverse-square law, so doubling distance gives one quarter the force.
One half comes from treating the law as inverse-linear.

items.prompt: What does the magnetic field around a long straight wire carrying current look like?

options.label: Closed circles around the wire
No field exists unless the wire is coiled
Straight lines running parallel to the wire
Lines pointing radially outward from the wire

rubric: The field forms closed circles around the wire, with direction given by the right-hand rule.
Radial lines describe an electric field of a charged wire, and coiling only strengthens the field.

items.prompt: A wire is replaced by one of the same material and thickness but twice as long. What happens to its resistance?

options.label: It stays the same
It doubles
It quadruples
It halves

rubric: Resistance is proportional to length, R = rho L / A, so doubling length doubles resistance.
Halving or quadrupling comes from mixing up the length and area dependence.

items.prompt: Why does pushing a bar magnet into a coil of wire produce a brief current?

options.label: A magnet always pushes electrons along any wire near it
The coil becomes a permanent magnet once the magnet enters
The flux through the coil changes, which induces an emf
The magnet's field adds charge to the wire

rubric: A changing flux through the coil induces an emf, which drives the current.
A steady field near a wire does not push charges, and a magnet adds no charge.

items.prompt: A magnet moves through a coil, inducing an emf. Which changes would increase the induced emf? Select all that apply.

options.label: Moving the magnet through faster
Using a stronger magnet
Using a coil with more turns
Holding the magnet still inside the coil

rubric: Induced emf grows with turns and with the rate of flux change, which rises with speed and magnet strength.
A stationary magnet gives no changing flux, so no emf is induced.

items.prompt: In a lab, a proton enters a region of uniform magnetic field moving perpendicular to the field lines. No other forces act on it. Which describes its motion in the field?

options.label: It moves in a circle at constant speed
It moves in a straight line and speeds up
It moves in a straight line at constant speed
It follows a parabola like a projectile

rubric: The magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity, so it changes direction but not speed, giving circular motion.
Straight-line or parabolic motion would need a force along the velocity or a constant-direction force.

items.prompt: Two small like charges repel each other with force F. The distance between them is doubled and the charges are unchanged. What happens to the force?

options.label: It doubles to 2F
It stays equal to F
It falls to one quarter of F
It falls to one half of F

rubric: Coulomb's force varies as 1/r^2, so doubling r gives F/4.
Choosing one half treats the force as inversely proportional to distance, not distance squared.

items.prompt: Which description fits the electric field lines around an isolated negative point charge?

options.label: They point outward and start at the charge
They form closed circles around the charge
They point inward and end on the charge
They run parallel and never meet the charge

rubric: Field lines show the force on a positive test charge, which is pulled toward a negative charge.
Outward lines describe a positive charge; closed loops describe magnetic fields.

items.prompt: A solid metal sphere sits in an electrostatic equilibrium. Why is the electric field inside the metal zero?

options.label: Free charges move until the net force on them vanishes
Fields cancel only at the center, not elsewhere inside
Excess charge spreads evenly through the entire volume
The metal blocks all fields because it contains no charges

rubric: Free charges rearrange until the internal field is zero; otherwise they would keep moving.
Excess charge sits on the surface, not through the volume, and metals do contain mobile charges.

items.prompt: A 2 ohm resistor and a 6 ohm resistor are connected in series to a battery. How do the currents through them compare?

options.label: The 2 ohm resistor carries more, since it resists less
They are equal, since charge has only one path through both
Each carries half, since the current splits at the junction
The 6 ohm resistor carries more, since it drops more voltage

rubric: In series there is a single path, so the current is the same everywhere.
The other options confuse series with parallel, where current splits and the smaller resistance carries more.

items.prompt: A positive charge moves in a straight line parallel to a uniform magnetic field. What magnetic force acts on it?

options.label: Zero, since only the velocity component across the field counts
Maximum, since the charge moves along the field direction
Opposite its motion, since the field slows moving charges
Along its motion, since the field pushes it forward

rubric: The magnetic force is q v x B, which vanishes when v is parallel to B.
Magnetic forces are perpendicular to velocity and do no work, so they never speed up or slow a charge.

items.prompt: Which statements about Faraday's law of induction are correct? Select all that apply.

options.label: An emf is induced when the magnetic flux through a loop changes
A loop rotating in a uniform field can have an induced emf
A loop at rest in a steady uniform field has no induced emf
A strong steady field alone induces a large emf in a loop

rubric: Induced emf depends on the rate of change of flux, which rotation can produce.
Field strength alone does not induce emf; the flux must change.

items.prompt: A student pushes a bar magnet's north pole toward a coil connected to a galvanometer. The needle deflects. She holds the magnet still inside the coil and the needle returns to zero. What explains this?

options.label: Flux through the coil changed only while the magnet moved
The magnet's field vanishes when the magnet stops moving
The coil's resistance rises once the magnet is inside it
Current needs the magnet to touch the coil's wires

rubric: Emf appears only while flux is changing; a steady flux gives zero emf.
Static magnets still have fields; the other options invent effects unrelated to induction.

items.prompt: Point charges of 2 microcoulombs and 3 microcoulombs are 0.30 m apart. Using k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2, what is the force between them?
rubric: 0.18 N results from dividing by r instead of r^2.

items.prompt: What is the magnitude of the electric field 3.0 m from a point charge of 4.0 nC? Use k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2.

options.label: 12 N/C
36 N/C

rubric: 12 N/C divides by r instead of r^2; 36 N/C forgets to divide by r^2.

items.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 ohm and a 2 ohm resistor in series. What is the voltage across the 4 ohm resistor?

options.label: 6 V
8 V
4 V

rubric: Current is 12/6 = 2 A, so V = 2 x 4 = 8 V.
6 V assumes the voltage splits equally regardless of resistance.

items.prompt: A 6 ohm and a 3 ohm resistor are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?

options.label: 2 ohm
4.5 ohm
9 ohm
1 ohm

rubric: 9 ohm adds them as if in series; 4.5 ohm takes the average.

items.prompt: A particle with charge 2.0 microcoulombs moves at 500 m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.40 T magnetic field. What is the magnetic force on it?
rubric: Other values come from mishandling the micro prefix or misusing the factors.

items.prompt: A flat loop sits face-on to a magnetic field that changes with time. Using emf = N A (dB/dt), which changes would double the induced emf? Select all that apply.

options.label: Doubling B while keeping it constant in time
Doubling the number of turns N
Doubling the loop area A
Halving the time over which B changes by the same amount

rubric: The emf is proportional to N, A and dB/dt, so doubling any one doubles it.
A constant B has dB/dt = 0, so scaling it gives no emf.

items.prompt: A single-turn circular loop of area 0.20 m^2 lies perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The field rises steadily from 0 to 0.50 T in 0.10 s. What average emf is induced in the loop?
rubric: emf = A x change in B / time = 0.20 x 0.50 / 0.10 = 1.0 V.
0.50 V or 10 V come from dropping or misplacing a factor in the ratio.

items.prompt: A point charge of +3.0 µC and a point charge of -5.0 µC are 0.30 m apart in vacuum. Using k = 8.99 x 10^9 N·m²/C², what is the electric force between them?

options.label: 1.5 N, repulsive
4.5 N, attractive
1.5 N, attractive
0.45 N, attractive

rubric: F = k|q1 q2|/r² = 8.99e9 x 15e-12 / 0.09 ≈ 1.5 N, and opposite charges attract.
Distractors target a sign error on the direction and slips in the r² or microcoulomb arithmetic.

items.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area 0.020 m² and separation 1.0 mm with vacuum between the plates (ε0 = 8.85 x 10^-12 F/m). It is charged to 100 V. How much energy does it store?
rubric: C = ε0A/d = 1.77e-10 F, so U = ½CV² = 8.85e-7 J.
Distractors come from forgetting the factor ½ or mis-handling the powers of ten in the 1 mm gap.

items.prompt: A 12 V ideal battery drives a 6 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of a 3 Ω and a 6 Ω resistor. What is the current through the 3 Ω resistor?
rubric: The parallel pair is 2 Ω, so total is 8 Ω and I = 1.5 A; the pair has 3 V across it, giving 1.0 A in the 3 Ω resistor.
Distractors confuse the total current with the branch current or split the current equally between the branches.

items.prompt: A proton (m = 1.67 x 10^-27 kg, q = 1.60 x 10^-19 C) moves at 2.0 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.50 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its circular path?

options.label: 4.2 cm
8.4 cm
2.1 cm

rubric: Distractors arise from dropping or doubling a factor, such as using 2B or v/2.

items.prompt: A flat coil of 50 turns and area 0.050 m² has its plane perpendicular to a uniform field. The field rises steadily from 0 to 0.40 T in 0.20 s. What is the magnitude of the induced emf?
rubric: Distractors omit the number of turns or mishandle the time interval.

items.prompt: A uniformly charged solid insulating sphere has total charge Q and radius R. Which of these field magnitudes, found with Gauss's law, are correct? Select all that apply.

options.label: At r = R/2, E = 4kQ/R²
At r = 2R, E = kQ/(2R²)
At r = R/2, E = kQ/(2R²)
At r = 2R, E = kQ/(4R²)

rubric: Outside, E = kQ/r²; inside, only the enclosed charge Q(r/R)³ counts, so E = kQr/R³.
Distractors wrongly use the full charge inside the sphere or mis-square the distance.

items.prompt: A conducting rod of length 0.40 m slides at a constant 3.0 m/s along two parallel rails joined by a resistor, in a uniform 0.50 T field perpendicular to the rail plane. The total circuit resistance is 0.20 Ω, and friction is negligible. What external force is needed to keep the rod moving at constant speed?
rubric: emf = BLv = 0.60 V, I = 3.0 A, and the magnetic drag is BIL = 0.60 N, which the applied force must balance.
Distractors come from using the emf as the force or dropping a factor in B, I or L.

items.prompt: A student applies Gauss's law with a cylindrical surface to find E at 0.40 m from the middle of a charged rod only 0.50 m long, and the answer disagrees with direct integration. Which diagnosis is best?

options.label: Gauss's law holds only for spherical charge distributions, so a cylindrical surface is invalid
Gauss's law fails for line charges because the charge has no volume to enclose
The rod is too short for cylindrical symmetry, so E cannot be pulled out of the flux integral
The end caps carry flux only if the rod is a conductor, so they must be added

rubric: Gauss's law is always true, but it gives E easily only when symmetry makes E constant over the surface; a short rod lacks that symmetry.
Distractors wrongly blame the law itself rather than the missing symmetry.

items.prompt: A magnet dropped down a vertical copper tube falls much more slowly than one dropped down a plastic tube of the same size. Which explanation is best?

options.label: The magnet induces static charges on the copper that repel it with a constant force
Induced currents appear only when the magnet is at rest, and they hold it against gravity
Changing flux drives eddy currents in the copper whose field opposes the magnet's motion and dissipates energy
Copper is ferromagnetic, so it pulls the magnet upward with a steady force

rubric: Lenz's law: the moving magnet changes the flux, and the induced eddy currents oppose that change, giving a speed-dependent drag.
Distractors treat the effect as static magnetism or static charge rather than induction from motion.

items.prompt: Three identical bulbs: A is in series with a parallel pair B and C, all connected to an ideal battery. Bulb B burns out and becomes an open circuit. Compared with before, what happens to A and C?

options.label: Both A and C dim
A dims and C brightens
Both stay the same
A brightens and C dims

rubric: Total resistance rises from 1.5R to 2R, so the current through A falls; C now carries all of that current, which exceeds its earlier half share.
Distractors ignore that C's share changes or assume the battery keeps each bulb's current fixed.

items.prompt: A student says: "At the midpoint between two equal +q charges the electric field is zero, so the potential there is zero too." Which statement identifies the flaw?

options.label: Field and potential are unrelated, so nothing can be inferred about one from the other
Potential is a scalar sum, so the two positive contributions add and V is not zero even though E is
Potential is a vector sum, so the two contributions cancel only if the charges are opposite
Potential there is zero only if both charges are at equal distances from a grounded point

rubric: E is a vector sum that cancels at the midpoint, but V is a scalar sum of two positive terms, so V is nonzero; E = -dV/dx only means V is at an extremum.
Distractors treat V as a vector or claim V and E are unrelated.

items.prompt: A charged parallel-plate capacitor is disconnected from its battery, and then a dielectric slab is slid fully between the plates. How do the plate charge Q, the voltage V and the stored energy U change?

options.label: Q falls, V falls, U falls
Q stays constant, V stays constant, U rises
Q rises, V stays constant, U rises
Q stays constant, V falls, U falls

rubric: The isolated plates keep Q fixed; C rises by the dielectric constant, so V = Q/C and U = Q²/2C both fall.
Distractors apply the battery-connected case (V fixed) or let charge leak off an isolated capacitor.

items.prompt: A flat conducting loop sits in a uniform magnetic field with its plane initially perpendicular to the field. Which actions induce an emf in the loop? Select all that apply.

options.label: Squeezing the loop so its area shrinks
Rotating it about a diameter that lies in the loop plane, perpendicular to B
Rotating it about an axis parallel to B through its center
Moving it at a steady velocity through the uniform field

rubric: An emf needs a changing flux BA cosθ; rotating about a diameter perpendicular to B changes θ, and shrinking the loop changes A.
Steady translation in a uniform field or spinning about the field axis leaves the flux unchanged.

items.prompt: Two conducting spheres of radius 1.0 cm and 4.0 cm are far apart and joined by a long thin wire. A total charge Q is placed on the system and allowed to reach equilibrium. A student compares the electric field just outside the surfaces of the two spheres. Which statement is correct?

options.label: The fields are equal because each sphere holds the same charge
The field at the large sphere is greater because it holds more charge
The field at the small sphere is 4 times larger, since equal V gives charge proportional to R and E = V/R
The fields are equal because the spheres are at the same potential

rubric: Equal potentials give q = 4πε0VR, and the surface field is E = V/R, so the smaller sphere has the stronger field.
Distractors confuse equal potential with equal field, or assume a larger charge means a larger field.

items.prompt: A point charge q sits exactly at one corner of an imaginary cube. Using Gauss's law and symmetry, what is the electric flux through one of the three faces that do NOT touch that corner?
rubric: Total flux through the cube is q/(8ε0), shared equally by the three far faces, giving q/(24ε0); the faces at the corner get zero.
q/(6ε0) assumes the charge is at the cube's centre; q/(8ε0) is the whole cube.

items.prompt: A neutral, isolated, spherical conducting shell has a point charge +q placed off-centre inside its cavity. Which description of the induced surface charge is correct?

options.label: Inner and outer surfaces: both uniform, since the shell itself is a sphere
Inner surface: -q, nonuniform. Outer surface: +q, nonuniform, since the inside field is asymmetric
Inner surface: -q, nonuniform. Outer surface: +q, uniform, since the cavity field is screened
Inner surface: -q, uniform. Outer surface: +q, nonuniform, since the charge is off-centre

rubric: The inner charge pattern must cancel the field in the metal and so is nonuniform; the outer surface only sees the shielded total +q and spreads it uniformly.
Distractors assume the outer surface 'remembers' the off-centre position.

items.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor is charging with wire current I. Applying Ampère's law (without Maxwell's term) to a loop around the wire gives different answers for a flat surface between the plates and a bulging surface cutting the wire. What resolves the contradiction?

options.label: Only flat surfaces are permitted in Stokes' theorem, so the bulging one is invalid
The changing electric flux in the gap acts as a displacement current equal to I
Ampère's law only holds for steady currents, so Biot–Savart must replace it here
The magnetic field in the gap is zero because no charge crosses it

rubric: Displacement current ε0 dΦE/dt equals I in the gap, so both surfaces give the same circulation of B.
Distractors misread the failure as one of the surface or of the law's scope rather than a missing term.

items.prompt: A 2 A current flows through a 0.5 H inductor. A mechanical switch in series is opened and a bright arc appears across its contacts. What best explains the arc?

options.label: The inductor's resistance jumps, so the full supply voltage appears across the switch
The supply voltage doubles when the circuit opens because the resistance drops
The inductor's emf, L dI/dt, becomes very large as the current is forced to fall quickly
The switch capacitance charges to the supply voltage, and discharges as a spark

rubric: The inductor opposes the rapid change in current with emf L dI/dt, which can far exceed the supply voltage.
Other options invoke source or capacitive effects that cannot produce a spike beyond the supply.

items.prompt: A magnet is dropped through a closed aluminium ring and falls slowly. Through an identical ring with a narrow saw cut, it falls almost freely. What explains the difference?

options.label: The cut ring is lighter, so gravity dominates the magnetic force by comparison
An emf still appears in the cut ring, but no current flows, so there is no opposing force
The cut removes the aluminium's conductivity, so no flux can pass through it
Cutting the ring cancels the changing flux through it, so no emf appears at all

rubric: Changing flux still induces an emf around the gap, but with no closed path there is no current and no Lenz braking force.
Distractors confuse emf with current or claim the flux changes differently.

items.prompt: A solid, uncharged-current conductor of irregular shape holds a net charge and is in electrostatic equilibrium. Which statements must be true? Select all that apply.

options.label: The electric field inside the conducting material is zero
Net charge is spread uniformly through the volume
The conductor's surface is an equipotential
Surface charge density is the same everywhere on the surface
The potential inside the material differs from the surface potential

rubric: Equilibrium requires E=0 inside, so the potential is constant throughout and equal to the surface value.
Charge density concentrates at sharp points, and excess charge resides on the surface, not in the volume.

items.prompt: A rectangular loop, 0.2 m wide, moves at a constant 3 m/s into a large region of uniform field B = 0.5 T perpendicular to the loop. Once the loop is completely inside, a student claims the emf is 0.3 V because the two sides cut field lines. What is the correct analysis of the emf around the loop?

options.label: The emf is zero, since a uniform field exerts no magnetic force on the moving charges
The emf is 0.15 V, since only one side is still cutting field lines
The emf is 0.3 V, since each side's contribution adds around the loop
The emf is zero, since flux is constant and the motional emfs in the two sides cancel around the loop

rubric: Both sides generate vBL but in opposite senses around the loop, so they cancel, consistent with constant flux.
The force qv×B does exist in each side; the net emf vanishes through cancellation, not absence of force.

items.prompt: A sensor must be screened from 50 Hz magnetic fields of a nearby transformer and from stray static electric fields, using one thin-walled enclosure. Which option best meets both criteria?

options.label: A plastic box with dense walls, since insulators absorb both field types
A thick glass box, since high dielectric constant cancels external fields
A thin copper foil box, since skin depth at 50 Hz blocks the magnetic field
A grounded high-permeability alloy box, which shunts low-frequency flux and screens electric fields

rubric: Copper skin depth at 50 Hz is about 9 mm, so foil fails for magnetic fields; a high-permeability alloy guides the flux and a grounded metal screens E.
Insulators do not shield either field type.

items.prompt: A student argues: 'E is zero inside a conductor in equilibrium, so the electric potential inside it must be zero as well.' Judge this reasoning.

options.label: Valid, since the potential is the integral of E and so vanishes where E vanishes
Valid, since conductors are always grounded at equilibrium by definition
Invalid, since the potential is constant throughout but may be any value set by the charge and surroundings
Invalid, since the potential inside varies linearly while the field stays zero

rubric: Zero field means zero gradient, so V is constant, not necessarily zero; the reference is arbitrary.
Distractors confuse zero gradient with zero value.

items.prompt: You need the electric field at an arbitrary point off the axis of a uniformly charged finite disc. Judge the approaches by whether they are valid and practical. Which is best?

options.label: Gauss's law with a spherical surface, since the disc is roughly round
Gauss's law with a cylindrical pillbox, since the disc is flat
Direct superposition by integrating over ring or area elements, since no Gaussian surface gives a symmetry shortcut
Use V = kq/r with the total charge, since distance dominates the field

rubric: Gauss's law only yields E when symmetry makes E constant over the surface; a finite disc off-axis lacks it, so integration is needed.
The distractors misuse symmetry or treat the disc as a point charge.

items.prompt: A solenoid on a fixed-voltage supply must have its central field B doubled. Criteria: same wire, same coil length and radius, and B must be doubled, not more. Which modification best meets this?

options.label: Wind twice the turns in an extra layer, since n doubles
Insert a linear core with relative permeability 2, leaving the current unchanged
Halve the coil length keeping all turns, since n doubles
Use wire of twice the diameter, since the current then doubles

rubric: A core with μr=2 doubles B at unchanged current. Doubling turns doubles wire length and R, halving I, so B is unchanged.
Halving the length or doubling diameter raises I and n, giving about four times B.

items.prompt: A dielectric slab is slid fully into a charged parallel-plate capacitor. Which judgement about the stored energy is correct?

options.label: It rises in both cases, because capacitance increases
It falls in both cases, because the field inside is reduced
It falls if the battery stays connected, and rises if the capacitor is isolated
It rises if the battery stays connected, and falls if the capacitor is isolated

rubric: At fixed V, U = CV^2/2 rises with C; at fixed Q, U = Q^2/2C falls as C rises.
Distractors apply one constraint to both cases or swap them.

items.prompt: Judge these claims about the Maxwell equations at an introductory level. Which are valid? Select all that apply.

options.label: Ampère's law without the displacement term stays consistent for a charging capacitor
Faraday's law implies the electric field from a changing B is non-conservative, so a single potential cannot describe it
A static electric field can have nonzero curl, if the charge density is nonzero
Gauss's law for magnetism implies the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero

rubric: Changing B gives circulation of E, so the field is not curl-free; no magnetic monopoles means zero net flux through closed surfaces.
Static E fields have zero curl, and the displacement term is needed for charging capacitors.

items.prompt: An engineer designs a 50 Hz transformer core. The criteria are to carry the magnetic flux well while minimising eddy-current heating. A solid iron block is cheap but runs hot. Which redesign best meets both criteria?

options.label: Thin iron sheets stacked parallel to the flux and insulated from each other, which interrupts eddy loops
A thicker solid iron core, since greater cross-section lowers the flux density
A solid copper core, since higher conductivity lowers the dissipated power
Thin iron sheets stacked perpendicular to the flux, which interrupts the flux path

rubric: Insulated laminations parallel to the flux keep the flux path in iron while confining eddy loops to thin cross-sections, cutting loss.
Higher conductivity increases eddy currents, and sheets across the flux obstruct it.

items.prompt: A student claims: "If the net electric flux through a closed surface is zero, the electric field must be zero at every point on that surface." Which critique is best justified by Gauss's law?

options.label: The claim is correct, because charges outside a closed surface always produce zero field at every point on that surface.
The claim is wrong, because only spherical surfaces give zero net flux, and any other shape always gives nonzero net flux.
The claim is correct, because Gauss's law forces E·dA to vanish at every point whenever the enclosed charge is zero.
The claim is wrong, because zero net flux only means inward and outward flux cancel, so E can be large locally, as on a surface around a dipole.

rubric: Gauss's law constrains only the integral of E·dA, so cancellation between inward and outward flux is allowed.
Distractors confuse zero net flux with zero local field, or mistake shape dependence for the cause.

items.prompt: A student argues that a rectangular conducting loop moving at constant velocity through a region of uniform, static magnetic field (loop entirely inside the field) must carry a steady current, because every charge in it feels v×B. Which evaluation is best?

options.label: Flawed: flux through the loop stays constant, so net emf is zero, since the motional emfs on opposite sides oppose around the loop.
Valid: the v×B force on each side drives current around the loop, so the side emfs add up to a nonzero total.
Valid: the loop's kinetic energy must be converted into current, so a steady current flows and slows the loop down.
Flawed: a uniform field exerts no force on charges in a moving conductor, so no emf appears even in an individual segment.

rubric: Constant flux means zero net emf; opposite sides have equal motional emfs that cancel around the circuit.
Distractors assume the side emfs add, or deny that any force or emf exists in individual segments.

items.prompt: A designer must justify the shielding capability of a closed, thick copper box for sensitive electronics. Which statement about its effect on external static fields is best justified?

options.label: It shields neither static field, because only time-varying fields can induce the eddy currents that provide any cancellation inside.
It shields static magnetic fields but not static electric fields, because free charges in copper cannot respond to a steady electric field.
It shields static electric fields, because charges rearrange until the interior field is zero, but it does not shield static magnetic fields.
It shields static electric and static magnetic fields equally, because surface charges and surface currents both rearrange to cancel the interior field.

rubric: Mobile charges redistribute until E inside the conductor is zero; a nonmagnetic conductor has no comparable response to static B.
Distractors treat E and B shielding as symmetric or deny the electrostatic response.

items.prompt: You need a small probe to measure a steady 20 mT field near a permanent magnet. Criterion: the reading must be proportional to the field itself, not its rate of change. Which choice is best justified?

options.label: Either probe equally, because induced emf in both depends only on the magnitude of the field present.
A search coil with many turns, because emf grows with N and area even when the field is not changing.
A search coil, because Faraday induction responds to the flux itself rather than to its rate of change.
A Hall probe, because its output voltage is proportional to B itself, whereas a fixed search coil's emf is proportional to dB/dt and is zero here.

rubric: Hall voltage scales with B directly, so it works for DC fields; a stationary coil sees emf = -N dΦ/dt = 0.
Distractors misread Faraday's law as depending on flux itself.

items.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor stays connected to a battery of voltage V while a dielectric slab is slowly drawn in, raising capacitance by ΔC. Which energy accounting is best?

options.label: The battery supplies ΔC·V^2, all of it stored, so the stored energy rises by ΔC·V^2.
The battery supplies nothing because V is constant; the rise in stored energy comes entirely from the slab's motion.
The battery supplies ½ΔC·V^2, all of it stored, and drawing the slab in costs no further energy.
The battery supplies ΔC·V^2; half raises the stored energy and half appears as mechanical work as the field draws the slab in.

rubric: Charge increases by ΔC·V, so battery work is ΔC·V^2, while stored energy rises only by ½ΔC·V^2; the remainder is mechanical work.
Distractors ignore the battery's work or assume all of it is stored.

items.prompt: Evaluate each statement about Maxwell's equations and pick the valid ones. Select all that apply.

options.label: Because curl E = 0 when B is static, the line integral of a static electric field around any closed path is zero.
Without the displacement-current term, Ampère's law would be inconsistent with charge conservation near a charging capacitor.
Field lines leaving a bar magnet's north pole show that Gauss's law for magnetism (div B = 0) is violated.
A uniform, constant electric field in vacuum must be accompanied by a magnetic field through the displacement term.

rubric: Displacement current rescues consistency with continuity, and curl E = 0 for static B makes electrostatic fields conservative.
Field lines of a magnet form closed loops, and the displacement term needs a changing E, not a constant one.

items.prompt: A 50 Hz power transformer with a solid iron core runs hot at no load, even though the winding resistance is small. An engineer must judge remedies using the criterion of cutting core heating while keeping a good flux path. Which remedy is best justified?

options.label: Swap to a solid copper core, because its higher conductivity lets eddy currents flow with less resistive loss.
Use a thicker solid iron core, because the larger cross-section lowers flux density so eddy currents largely vanish.
Use thin insulated laminations, because they break up eddy-current loops and cut I^2R heating while keeping the flux path.
Raise the operating frequency, because the flux changes less per cycle and so induces smaller circulating currents.

rubric: Lamination limits loop area for induced currents, reducing eddy-current loss without disrupting flux.
Distractors raise conductivity, area or frequency, all of which increase eddy currents.

items.prompt: Design two identical coaxial circular coils of radius R carrying equal currents in the same direction, so the on-axis field near the midpoint is as uniform as possible (second derivative of B vanishes there). What coil separation meets this?

options.label: R
2R

rubric: Separation equal to R (Helmholtz configuration) makes d²B/dz² zero at the midpoint.
Other spacings leave a dip or peak at the center.

items.prompt: Design a cable for a low-level sensor 50 m from a motor drive that emits time-varying magnetic fields. Constraints: use only one two-wire pair, no heavy magnetic shielding, and minimize induced pickup. Which design meets them?

options.label: Coil the cable into a tight spool, so the added turns raise the signal relative to the induced noise.
Use one wire with a chassis ground return, so the loop area is large and pickup averages out.
Twist the pair tightly and read it differentially, so emfs induced in adjacent loops cancel and common noise is rejected.
Run the two wires widely separated along the route, so the signal and return paths avoid sharing noise.

rubric: Twisting makes successive loops oppose in induced emf, and differential reading removes common-mode pickup.
Distractors enlarge the loop area or add turns, which increases induced emf.

items.prompt: Design a velocity selector passing singly charged ions at 2×10^5 m/s through a uniform B = 0.01 T. Which electric-field choice meets the requirement?

options.label: E = 20 V/m, perpendicular to both v and B, so electric and magnetic forces oppose each other
E = 2000 V/m, perpendicular to both v and B, so electric and magnetic forces cancel
E = 2000 V/m, parallel to B, so the electric force opposes the magnetic force on the particle
E = 2×10^7 V/m, perpendicular to both v and B, so electric and magnetic forces oppose each other

rubric: Cancellation needs qE = qvB, so E = vB = 2000 V/m, perpendicular to v and B.
Distractors use a wrong magnitude or a field that cannot oppose v×B.

items.prompt: A proposed wireless charger has a transmit coil driven by a steady DC supply and a nearby receive coil wired to a battery. Which change supplies the missing element so power can be transferred?

options.label: Raise the DC current greatly, so the flux through the receiver grows large enough to keep inducing a steady emf.
Move the coils closer together, so the constant flux linkage between them drives a continuous current.
Add an iron core inside the receive coil, so the steady flux there induces a steady emf.
Drive the transmit coil with oscillating current, so the flux through the receiver changes and induces an emf.

rubric: Induction needs a changing flux, so the transmitter must carry time-varying current.
Distractors try to enlarge a constant flux, which still induces no steady emf.

items.prompt: To find E inside an infinite slab of uniform charge density ρ and thickness d, you must design a Gaussian surface exploiting the symmetry. Which surface is the best choice?

options.label: A cube tilted 45° to the slab faces, so every face receives the same flux.
A long cylinder whose axis lies parallel to the slab surface, so E is constant along its side.
A pillbox centered on the slab's midplane, with end caps parallel to the faces, so E is uniform and perpendicular on the caps.
A sphere centered on a point in the slab, so the field is constant over its curved surface.

rubric: Planar symmetry makes E perpendicular to the slab and equal at mirrored heights, so a symmetric pillbox gives E directly.
Distractors use shapes that do not match planar symmetry.

items.prompt: A generator's peak emf is NBAω. You must double the peak emf while keeping the same magnet and the same coil area. Which modifications meet this constraint? Select all that apply.

options.label: Double the rotation rate of the coil.
Double the resistance of the connected load.
Double the number of turns on the coil.
Reverse the rotation direction of the coil.

rubric: With B and A fixed, peak emf scales with N and ω, so doubling either doubles it.
Load resistance changes current, not the emf, and reversing rotation only flips the sign.

items.prompt: You must measure 50 Hz currents up to several kA in a busbar. Constraints: no electrical contact, the busbar cannot be cut, and the sensor must not saturate at high current. Which design meets all of them?

options.label: Wind an air-core toroidal coil around the busbar and integrate its induced emf, which is proportional to dI/dt.
Lay a straight wire alongside the busbar and measure the voltage between its ends.
Clamp an iron-core current transformer around the busbar and read its secondary current directly.
Insert a low-resistance series shunt and measure the voltage across it.

rubric: An air-core coil (Rogowski type) has emf proportional to dI/dt, needs no contact or cut, and cannot saturate; integration recovers I.
Distractors need cutting the bar, risk core saturation, or couple poorly.
